item.title: 4 episode(s) — 5:32pm 24/Nov
item.description:
Interviewees:

  • Ellen Sandell, Greens leader (ABC Radio National Breakfast; ABC Politics Now)
  • Mike Isaac, tech reporter, New York Times / Atlantic (ABC Radio National Breakfast)
  • Jared Lynch, tech editor (The Front)
  • Yasmin Satta, founder, Rohingya Myeik-Foyna Collaborative Network (Full Story)
  • Camille Ahmed, journalist, Guardian (inferred) (Full Story)
  • Melissa Clark, journalist (ABC Politics Now)

Key Themes:

  • Economic policy, inflation, and budget management — ABC Politics Now focused deeply on the political and fiscal details of the mid-year budget update and net savings, while other episodes touched on broader macroeconomic trends.
  • Corporate governance and geopolitical pressure in the tech sector — RN Breakfast provided a concise news wrap of Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia, whereas The Front offered a deep-dive analysis into the chaotic political influence exerted by Donald Trump and JD Vance.
  • Victorian politics and minor party electoral prospects — RN Breakfast briefly examined minor party viability in a morning news format, whereas ABC Politics Now conducted a more extended assessment of Green Party polling and strategic positioning.
  • International justice, genocide rulings, and human rights — Full Story delivered an in-depth standalone feature examining the ICJ ruling on Myanmar and its broader geopolitical implications.

Key Actors:

  • Jensen Huang
  • Donald Trump
  • Jim Chalmers, Treasurer
  • Peter Dutton, Opposition Leader
  • Nvidia

Episodes in this run:

ABC Radio National Breakfast: Breakfast Wrap: Guess who's back? Jensen's back

  • Jensen Huang's return as CEO of Nvidia (00:40, 03:20) — Corporate governance and political pressure leading to Jensen Huang's reinstatement
    Voices: Luke Sidum-Dunstan (host, live); Donald Trump (former US President, clip); Mike Isaac (tech reporter, New York Times / Atlantic, pre-recorded interview); Jensen Huang (CEO, Nvidia, clip)
    Tone: Fascinated and explanatory, highlighting the rapid corporate and political turnaround
    Emphasis: Corporate strategy, political pressure from Trump, and the impact of artificial intelligence on the global economy
    Placement: Lead story, taking up the bulk of the segment
    “"It's a really fascinating move and basically stunned uh certainly stunned all of the business reporters out in Silicon Valley"”
  • Victorian State Election Preview (01:26, 01:50) — Can minor parties genuinely challenge Labor and the Liberals ahead of the Victorian election?
    Voices: Luke Sidum-Dunstan (host, live); Ellen Sandell (Greens leader, pre-recorded interview)
    Tone: Inquisitive and analytical, focusing on political competition and minor party viability
    Emphasis: Political strategy, minor party challenges, and electoral prospects in Victoria
    Placement: Second story in the breakfast wrap
    “"So can the minor parties genuinely challenge Labor and the Liberals?"”

The Front: Nvidia soaring: How Trump and Vance forced Nvidia to bring back Jensen Huang

  • Donald Trump's pressure on Nvidia regarding Jensen Huang (00:00, 07:51) — Political interference and corporate response in the US tech sector
    Voices: Claire Harvey (host, live); Jared Lynch (tech editor, live)
    Tone: Analytical, speculative, and conversational, exploring the chaotic nature of US politics and corporate governance
    Emphasis: Geopolitics, US political pressure on tech boards, and the risks of doing business in China
    Placement: Lead and sole deep-dive story of the episode
    “"Donald Trump seems to have ensured that the Nvidia board kind of got what they needed to reinstate Jensen Huang"”

Full Story: Myanmar has been found guilty of genocide. Should Israel be worried?

  • International Court of Justice ruling on Myanmar genocide against the Rohingya (00:00, 27:27) — Historic accountability for genocide and implications for international law and Israel
    Voices: Anushka Kelly (host, live); Rejaul Ahmed (journalist, live - inferred); Yasmin Satta (founder, Rohingya Myeik-Foyna Collaborative Network, pre-recorded interview); Camille Ahmed (journalist, Guardian, pre-recorded interview - inferred)
    Tone: Solemn, empathetic, and serious, focusing on justice for victims and the gravity of international legal rulings
    Emphasis: Human impact, refugee suffering, legal precedent, and global political consequences
    Placement: Full-length feature episode
    “"The UN's highest court is hearing a genocide case against Myanmar, the military's..."”

ABC Politics Now: It's operation 'smash inflation'

  • Jim Chalmers' mid-year budget update and economic strategy (00:00, 23:00) — Government economic policy aimed at smashing inflation through net savings
    Voices: Patricia Karvelas (host, live); Melissa Clark (journalist, live); Jim Chalmers (Treasurer, clip and archival); Peter Dutton (Opposition Leader, clip)
    Tone: Analytical, critical, and explanatory regarding fiscal policy and political positioning
    Emphasis: Cost of living, budget updates, inflation pressures, and political conflict between major parties
    Placement: Lead and primary story of the episode
    “"That was the grim warning offered by the Treasurer Jim Chalmers as he delivered his ministerial statement on the economy"”
  • Victorian Green Party poll results and electoral outlook (16:26, 06:01) — Green party prospects and minor party positioning ahead of the state election
    Voices: Patricia Karvelas (host, live); Ellen Sandell (Greens leader, pre-recorded interview)
    Tone: Inquisitive and politically focused
    Emphasis: Polling data, coalition dynamics, and voter sentiment in Victoria
    Placement: Second segment of the political roundup
    “"The Greens are confident of capitalizing on Labor's poor polling ahead of the vote on Saturday"”

item.title: 4 episode(s) — 9:31am 24/Nov

Key Themes:

  • Economic challenges and fiscal policy — News24 focused on the Treasurer's warnings of bigger budget deficits due to inflation, while other programs focused on social and health issues.
  • Mental health and maternal wellbeing — RN Breakfast explored the rise in postnatal depression rates and the need for better support and screening.
  • Political strategy and state elections — RN Breakfast examined the Victorian Greens' strategy to capitalise on Labor's poor standing ahead of the state election.
  • Social enterprise and community support — RN Breakfast highlighted how food can be used to drive social change and support marginalized communities.
  • Corporate governance and scandals — ABC AM focused on the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as NVIDIA chief following a scandal.

Key Actors:

  • Anthony Albanese, Prime Minister
  • Jensen Huang, NVIDIA president and CEO

item.title: 7 episode(s) — 8:02am 24/Nov
item.description:
Interviewees:

  • Blair Boyer, SA Minister for Health (ABC Radio National Breakfast)
  • Rob Watson, BBC World Service political correspondent (ABC Radio National Breakfast)
  • Isaac, technology reporter, Silicon Valley, Technology Reporter (ABC Radio National Breakfast)
  • Jim Chalmers, Federal Treasurer (ABC Radio National Breakfast)
  • Dr George Carter, Director of theANU Pacific Institute (ABC Radio National Breakfast)
  • Paige Taylor, political reporter, Political Reporter (The Front)
  • Sam Koslosky, co-host, Co-host (Daily Aus)
  • Emma Gillespie, co-host, Co-host (Daily Aus)

Key Themes:

  • Climate action and international climate talks (COP-31) — RN Breakfast focused on the Pacific nations' demands and strategic leverage, while Daily Aus explored broader international gridlock and fossil fuel lobbying.
  • Aged care crisis and hospital bed blockages
  • Post-Brexit UK-EU relations and trade deals
  • Corporate governance and technology leadership at Nvidia
  • Federal budget update and economic forecasts
  • Internal political conflict and identity politics within the Greens party

Key Actors:

  • Anthony Albanese, Prime Minister
  • Rishi Sunak, UK Prime Minister
  • Jensen Huang, Chief Executive of Nvidia
  • Jim Chalmers, Federal Treasurer
  • Blair Boyer, SA Minister for Health
  • Nicolette Bulla, Federal MP

Episodes in this run:

ABC Radio National Breakfast: SA demands action from federal government on aged care

  • South Australia demands federal action on aged care bed blockages (00:01, 05:43) — Aged care crisis in South Australia putting immense pressure on the broader health system and requiring immediate federal intervention.
    Voices: Presenter (live), Blair Boyer, SA Minister for Health (live)
    Tone: Urgent and explanatory. The presenter questioned the minister on systemic failures, while the minister framed the issue as a long-term demographic challenge requiring federal funding.
    Emphasis: Systemic strain, hospital bed blockages, and the human cost of elderly people waiting in emergency departments for residential aged care beds.
    Placement: Lead item, covering the top of the program.
    “We have known what the aging profile of Australia is going to be for a long, long time.”

ABC Radio National Breakfast: Does the new UK-EU deal signal the end of Brexit?

  • UK Prime Minister Rishi Sunak hails new UK-EU deal (00:01, 03:19) — Whether the new reset deal signals a significant shift in post-Brexit UK-EU relations or is merely a modest adjustment with limited economic impact.
    Voices: Presenter (live), Rob Watson, BBC World Service political correspondent (live)
    Tone: Analytical and skeptical. The presenter pressed on the practical limitations of the agreement, while the correspondent highlighted the political and trade hurdles.
    Emphasis: Trade impacts, political motivations, and the reality of post-Brexit economic friction.
    Placement: First main segment after headlines.
    “It's pretty modest in and every other way, and it's not going to change the world.”
  • Debate over UK-EU deal and future economic impacts (03:20, 03:10) — Assessing the political fallout and whether the deal marks a turning point or a permanent stagnation in UK-EU relations.
    Voices: Presenter (live), Rob Watson, BBC World Service political correspondent (live)
    Tone: Conversational and speculative, examining the political rhetoric versus economic reality.
    Emphasis: Political legacy, sovereignty concerns, and the difficulty of reversing Brexit-related friction.
    Placement: Second segment continuing the Brexit discussion.
    “The Brexit debate is back in a more general sense rather than just to do with this particular deal.”

ABC Radio National Breakfast: Jensen Huang reinstated as chief executive of Nvidia

  • Jensen Huang reinstated as chief executive of Nvidia (00:01, 04:36) — The stunning reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO following revelations of extra-marital affairs, highlighting the growing influence of AI and tech giants on global markets.
    Voices: Presenter (live), Isaac, technology reporter, Silicon Valley (live)
    Tone: Fascinated and bewildered. The presenter questioned the board's decision-making, while the reporter analyzed the broader implications for the tech industry.
    Emphasis: Corporate governance, executive power, and the dominance of artificial intelligence.
    Placement: Second main segment of the program.
    “It's a real fascinating move and basically stunned certainly stunned all of the business reporters out in Silicon Valley.”

ABC Radio National Breakfast: Treasurer flags 'substantial savings' in mid year budget update

  • Treasurer Jim Chalmers flags substantial savings in mid-year budget update (00:01, 06:55) — Treasurer Jim Chalmers forecasting softer economic growth, higher inflation, and higher unemployment while committing to savings and addressing structural budget challenges.
    Voices: Presenter (live), Jim Chalmers, Federal Treasurer (live)
    Tone: Direct and adversarial. The presenter challenged the Treasurer on the adequacy of savings and the economic outlook, while the Treasurer defended the government's fiscal strategy.
    Emphasis: Economic forecasts, cost-of-living pressures, inflation, and government spending restraint.
    Placement: Lead item on economic policy.
    “We've got to deal with some of the structural pressures on the budget.”

ABC Radio National Breakfast: Pacific was heard in COP-31 climate talks, Prime Minister Albanese says

  • Pacific nations make their voices heard at COP-31 climate talks (00:02, 06:30) — Assessment of the COP-31 climate talks outcome, focusing on the friction between Pacific nations demanding accelerated fossil fuel phase-outs and major economies pushing back.
    Voices: Presenter (live), Anthony Albanese, Prime Minister (clip), Dr George Carter, Director of theANU Pacific Institute (live)
    Tone: Serious and diplomatic. The presenter explored the geopolitical tensions, while the guest expert analyzed the Pacific's bargaining power.
    Emphasis: Climate diplomacy, fossil fuel phase-out commitments, and the strategic positioning of Pacific island states.
    Placement: Lead international and environmental segment.
    “Climate change is the first, second and third priority of Pacific leaders.”

The Front: ‘Fake Blak’: The Greens’ bitter civil war over Aboriginal identity

  • The Greens' bitter internal conflict over Aboriginal identity and 'Fake Blak' allegations (00:00, 20:00) — An in-depth investigative look into the internal turmoil within the Australian Greens party over allegations of cultural appropriation and Indigenous identity fraud.
    Voices: Presenter (live), Paige Taylor, political reporter (live)
    Tone: Investigative and somber. The presenter navigated a sensitive cultural issue with serious journalistic rigor.
    Emphasis: Party politics, Indigenous representation, authenticity standards, and internal party conflict.
    Placement: Standalone feature documentary episode.
    “Growing numbers of Greens members are identifying as Aboriginal, and they're getting a discount on their membership fees for ticking the box.”

Daily Aus: Has climate action stalled?

  • Analysis of COP-31 climate summit outcomes and international friction over fossil fuels (00:03, 15:00) — Evaluating whether global climate action has stalled following COP-31, examining the fierce debate between developed nations and oil producers over fossil fuel phase-out language.
    Voices: Presenter (live), Sam Koslosky, co-host (live), Emma Gillespie, co-host (live), Nicolette Bulla, Federal MP (clip)
    Tone: Analytical, accessible, and conversational. The hosts broke down complex international climate negotiations into relatable insights.
    Emphasis: International climate targets, diplomatic gridlock, fossil fuel lobbying, and the domestic political challenges of emissions reduction.
    Placement: Lead segment focusing on global environmental politics.
    “Almost 200 countries ran two days into overtime and still couldn't agree on whether those words belonged on the page.”

item.title: 6 episode(s) — 8:11pm 23/Nov
item.description:
Interviewees:

  • Dr Bill Hare, Physicist and climate scientist, CEO of Climate Analytics, CEO of Climate Analytics (ABC Radio National Breakfast)
  • Graham Readfearn, Climate and Environment Correspondent, Guardian Australia, Climate and Environment Correspondent (The Front; Full Story)
  • Jacob Greber, Journalist, Journalist (ABC Politics Now)
  • Romy Stevens, Environment Reporter, Environment Reporter (ABC AM)

Key Themes:

  • COP31 Climate Conference Collapse — AM focused on the immediate diplomatic breakdown; RN Breakfast and Full Story analyzed the geopolitical and fossil fuel lobbying dynamics; The Front emphasized the financial cost and national embarrassment; Politics Now examined the domestic political fallout.

Key Actors:

  • Chris Bowen, Minister for Climate Change and Energy
  • Dara O'Brien, Irish Minister for Climate

Episodes in this run:

ABC AM: COP31 ends in failure

  • COP31 Climate Conference Collapse (00:07, 03:30) — Global climate talks collapse without a deal over the future of fossil fuels.
    Voices: Isabella Higgins, Presenter (live); Dara O'Brien, Irish Minister for Climate (clip); Chris Bowen, Minister for Climate Change and Energy (live); Romy Stevens, Environment Reporter (live)
    Tone: Critical and disappointed, focusing on the failure to reach a consensus.
    Emphasis: Blame placed on oil-producing nations and geopolitical divisions.
    Placement: Lead item
    “00:15 - Major global climate talks have collapsed without a deal after a fierce debate about the future of fossil fuels.”

ABC Radio National Breakfast: Why did Cop31's climate talks collapse?

  • COP31 Climate Talks Breakdown (01:51, 02:35) — Explaining the deadlock and failure of the COP31 climate negotiations in Türkiye.
    Voices: David Speers, Presenter (live); Dara O'Brien, Irish Minister for Climate (clip); Chris Bowen, Minister for Climate Change and Energy (clip)
    Tone: Analytical and explanatory regarding the negotiations.
    Emphasis: Focus on the geopolitical divide between fossil fuel producers and the EU.
    Placement: Lead item
    “02:03 - The negotiations were the longest in cop history and several countries... declared that they couldn't accept a draft.”
  • Interview with Dr Bill Hare on COP31 Failure (04:18, 01:10) — Assessing the reasons behind the breakdown of the COP31 climate talks.
    Voices: David Speers, Presenter (live); Dr Bill Hare, Physicist and climate scientist, CEO of Climate Analytics (live)
    Tone: Adversarial and urgent, questioning Australia's role and the global failure.
    Emphasis: Focus on fossil fuel interests blocking progress.
    Placement: Second item
    “04:27 - The main thing for me is that the cover decision, the main decision has been blocked by a whole bunch of countries.”

The Front: Australia’s $150 million embarrassment at climate talks

  • Australia's Role and COP31 Failure (00:01, 03:45) — Australia faces criticism and financial embarrassment following the collapse of COP31.
    Voices: Claire Harvey, Presenter (live); Graham Readfearn, Climate and Environment Correspondent, Guardian Australia (live)
    Tone: Critical and reflective on Australia's diplomatic standing.
    Emphasis: Financial costs and diplomatic fallout.
    Placement: Lead item
    “00:07 - A global climate summit that's cost billions of dollars has collapsed in embarrassing failure, and Australia's getting the blame.”

Full Story: Cop31’s big fossil fuel failure

  • Deep Dive into COP31 Fossil Fuel Impasse (00:06, 10:15) — Examining why the fossil fuel phase-out language was stripped from the COP31 agreement.
    Voices: Nour Haydar, Presenter (live); Chris Bowen, Minister for Climate Change and Energy (clip); Graham Readfearn, Climate and Environment Correspondent, Guardian Australia (live)
    Tone: Analytical and investigative.
    Emphasis: The role of petrostates and international lobbying.
    Placement: Lead item
    “00:14 - Global climate talks in Türkiye have ended without a deal after a standoff between oil producing states and countries demanding a more ambitious response.”

ABC Politics Now: Good COP, bad COP

  • Political Fallout of COP31 for Australia (00:38, 08:15) — Analyzing the domestic political consequences of the COP31 failure for the Australian government.
    Voices: Patricia Karvelas, Presenter (live); Jacob Greber, Journalist (live)
    Tone: Political analysis and commentary.
    Emphasis: Domestic political pressure and international reputation.
    Placement: Lead item
    “00:39 - It was the longest cop on record and it ended with no deal.”

Daily Aus: Headlines: Jetstar class action update

  • Jetstar Class Action Lawsuit (00:18, 00:50) — Over a million Jetstar customers contacted over a class action lawsuit regarding COVID-19 flight cancellations.
    Voices: Presenter (unconfirmed)
    Tone: Informative and news-focused.
    Emphasis: Consumer rights and legal action.
    Placement: Lead item
    “00:18 - More than a million Jetstar customers are being contacted about a class action lawsuit against the airline.”
